questions.enonce_markdown:
State and explain one major use of the Internet which is peculiar to each of the following fields.

(a) Film industry. (2 marks)

(b) University. (2 marks)

(c) Telemedicine. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Film industry (2 marks).** *Online distribution and streaming of films.* Studios and distributors put films, series and trailers on the Internet (video on demand, for example Netflix or YouTube), so that viewers anywhere can watch them on demand without going to a cinema or buying a DVD; the Internet is also used to promote films (trailers, social media) and to share very large video files between studios in different countries during production and editing.

**(b) University (2 marks).** *E-learning and online research.* Lecturers publish notes, videos and assignments on a learning platform and run virtual classrooms (distance learning), so students can follow courses from anywhere; students and staff also use the Internet to search online libraries, journals and databases for research and to register or pay fees online.

**(c) Telemedicine (2 marks).** *Remote consultation and diagnosis.* A doctor examines and advises a patient in a distant village by video conference, or a local health worker sends X-rays, scans and test results over the Internet to a specialist in another town or country, who gives a diagnosis; patients' vital signs can also be monitored remotely, which saves travel time and cost and brings expert care to rural areas.

(Any one well explained use per field earns the marks: one mark for naming the use, one for the explanation.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Briefly explain the difference between simulation and prototyping. (2 marks)

(b) Describe two domain where each of the following is used.

- Simulation. (2 marks)
- Geographical Information System (GIS). (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Simulation and prototyping (2 marks).**

- **Simulation** is the use of a computer model to imitate the behaviour of a real system or process (a machine, an economy, the weather) so that it can be studied, tested or predicted safely, cheaply and quickly, without using the real thing.
- **Prototyping** is the building of an early, working but incomplete model (a prototype) of a new system or product so that users can try it, give feedback and correct the requirements before the final system is built; the prototype is refined and may become the final system.

In short, a simulation imitates how something *behaves* in order to experiment with it, while a prototype is a *first version* of the system itself that is shown to users and improved.

**(b) Domains of use (2 marks + 2 marks).**

*Simulation* (any two):

- Training: flight simulators for pilots, driving simulators, virtual surgery for medical students (mistakes cost nothing and nobody is at risk).
- Science and engineering: testing the behaviour of a bridge, aircraft or car (crash tests), nuclear or chemical processes before they are built or carried out.
- Weather and climate forecasting, and modelling the spread of a disease or the growth of a population.

*Geographical Information System (GIS)* (any two): a GIS stores, analyses and displays data linked to places on a map.

- Town and land-use planning: choosing sites for roads, schools or hospitals and managing land ownership.
- Environment and agriculture: mapping soil, forests, flood areas or crop yields, and monitoring natural disasters.
- Transport and navigation: finding the best route, tracking vehicles, mapping utility networks (water, electricity).
- Emergency services, defence and public health: locating incidents, planning rescue routes, mapping the spread of epidemics.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) In relation to an information system, what is a stock control system? (1 mark)

(b) Give two advantages of using a stock control system. (2 marks)

(c) State two main features of an expert system. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Stock control system (1 mark).** An information system that records and monitors the quantity of goods or materials held in stock, and the goods received and issued or sold, so that the right amount of each item is always available (it reports stock levels and signals when an item must be re-ordered).

**(b) Two advantages (2 marks)** (any two):

- It avoids both over-stocking (money tied up, goods expiring) and under-stocking (lost sales), because it triggers an automatic re-order when the stock of an item falls to its re-order level.
- It gives accurate, up-to-date information on stock at any moment, so managers take faster, better decisions and can produce reports.
- It reduces human errors and the time spent counting, and makes losses and theft easier to detect.

**(c) Two main features of an expert system (2 marks)** (any two):

- A **knowledge base** holding the facts and rules (the expertise) obtained from human experts in a particular field.
- An **inference engine** that applies the rules to the facts supplied by the user in order to reach a conclusion or advice.
- A question-and-answer **user interface** (and an explanation facility that shows how a conclusion was reached).
